spatial_claims.claim: Lines a and b meet at point O; r is perpendicular to both a and b at O
Plane π contains lines a and b (by 11.2)
Line r does not lie in plane π (proved by contradiction via 1.14)
Line r meets plane π only at O (by D1.7, 11.1)
Line t is in plane π through O, distinct from a and b
A ray of t is enclosed between chosen rays OB (on a) and OC (on b)
BC lies in plane π (by D1.7)
Angle from OB to ray of t is less than angle BOC (CN5)
t meets ray BC at point X; X is on segment BC so BX and BC are the same ray
A is on r distinct from O; A' is on opposite side of O with OA' = OA
Angles AOB, A'OB, AOC, A'OC are all right angles
AB = A'B and AC = A'C (by SAS via 1.4)
Triangles ABC and A'BC are congruent by SSS (1.8); angle ABC = angle A'BC
Since BX = BC (same ray), angle ABX = angle ABC and angle A'BX = angle A'BC
AX = A'X by SAS in triangles ABX and A'BX
Angle AOX = angle A'OX by SSS in triangles AOX and A'OX
A-O-A' collinear (on r), so angles AOX and A'OX are supplementary and equal, each 90 degrees

configuration_map: O is the intersection point of two distinct lines a, b lying in plane π. Line r passes through O perpendicular to both a and b; r is not in π and meets π only at O. Points A and A' lie on r on opposite sides of O with OA = OA'. An arbitrary line t in π through O has one ray enclosed between chosen rays OB (B on a) and OC (C on b). Point X is the intersection of t with segment BC, so X lies between B and C and BX/BC are the same ray. All triangles are planar by 11.2. The configuration is three-dimensional: A and A' are above and below π, while B, C, X, O all lie in π.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The betweenness of the ray of t between OB and OC is established by choosing the correct angular sector. The intersection X on segment BC follows validly from P5. The angle equalities (Steps 5-6) and segment equalities (Steps 4, 6) feed correctly into the final SSS congruence (Step 7). The supplementary-equal-angle argument at O is valid because A-O-A' are collinear on r and X is not on r. No pair of spatial claims contradicts any other.
